_help: THE voices for every @maddiee.makess reel (Option 3, chosen 2026-11-05). Never change the refs: every line is cloned from them so Maddie and Claude always sound the same. Per reel: copy this file to studio/voices/<scene>.json, fill 'jobs' (one per line, emotion tags like [sigh] [laughter] [surprise-oh] [surprise-wa] [question-en] [dissatisfaction-hnn] go inside the text), run the 'voices (OmniVoice)' workflow with that config, then put the wavs in codevid/voice/<scene>/NN.wav (render.js uses them automatically).

ref_text.maddie: Hey guys, I'm Maddie. Today I'll show you something crazy I made with my robot.
ref_text.claude: Good evening. I am Claude. I write the code, and I render the whole reel.

voices.maddie_C: male, teenager, moderate pitch, american accent
voices.claude_B: male, young adult, moderate pitch, british accent

jobs.text: [sigh] Four days since graduation...
and I've applied to sixty jobs.
Replies?
...Zero.
Because you sent the same resume, sixty times.
[dissatisfaction-hnn] What else am I supposed to do?!
Let a free tool do the boring part.
It's called career ops.
Eighty thousand stars on GitHub.
[surprise-wa] Eighty thousand?!
Step one. One line in Claude Code. Done.
Step two. It checks the career pages of a hundred plus companies.
Step three. Every job gets a score, one to five, against your C V.
And it flags the fake ones.
[question-en] Fake jobs?
Ghost postings. They exist. It skips them.
Step four. A new resume, for every job.
A T S friendly. Plus the cover letter.
Step five. It fills the whole form.
And submits it?
No. You press submit. Your name, your call.
Everything goes in one tracker. Free. Open source.
So I just... press it?
Yes. Hardest thing you'll do this week.
[laughter] Okay... I'm getting hired!
